# GAE Clinical Compass™
## Insurance Authorization Guide — Decision Support

Route: /gae/auth-guide

## Navigation
- Back to GAE Compass (→ /gae)
- Appeal Letter (→ /gae/appeal)

## Important: GAE Reimbursement Landscape
GAE reimbursement is highly variable across payers. Several major commercial insurers (notably Anthem/BCBS) classify GAE as experimental for musculoskeletal indications. Always verify coverage and obtain written authorization before scheduling. Use an ABN for Medicare patients and a financial responsibility waiver for commercial patients when coverage is uncertain.

## CPT Codes for GAE

### 37242 (RVU: ~8.5) — Primary code for GAE in knee osteoarthritis or chronic knee pain
Vascular embolization or occlusion, inclusive of all radiological supervision and interpretation, intraprocedural roadmapping, and imaging guidance necessary to complete the intervention — arterial, other than hemorrhage or tumor
Includes:
- All vascular access for the procedure
- Fluoroscopic guidance and roadmapping (bundled — do NOT bill separately)
- Radiologic supervision and interpretation
- Selective catheter placement to geniculate arteries
- Embolization of all targeted geniculate vessels in the same session
Note: This is the correct primary embolization code for GAE when performed for OA or knee pain. Some payers (Anthem, certain BCBS plans) classify this as experimental for musculoskeletal indications.

### 36245 (RVU: ~5.2) — Selective catheterization to geniculate artery branches (when separately billable)
Selective catheter placement, arterial system; each first-order abdominal, pelvic, or lower extremity artery branch
Includes:
- Initial selective catheter placement to the first-order vessel
Note: Bundled with 37242 under NCCI edits in many payer systems. Bill only when payer policy explicitly allows separate billing. Medicare typically does not reimburse for OA/knee pain diagnoses with this code.

### 36246 (RVU: ~2.5) — Second-order selective catheterization (e.g., descending genicular artery)
Selective catheter placement, arterial system; initial second-order abdominal, pelvic, or lower extremity artery branch
Includes:
- Additional selective catheter advancement to second-order vessel
Note: Subject to same bundling restrictions as 36245. Verify payer policy before billing.

### 37244 (RVU: ~9.0) — GAE for hemarthrosis (e.g., post-amputation bleed, traumatic hemarthrosis)
Vascular embolization or occlusion — for hemorrhage
Includes:
- All embolization services for hemorrhagic indication
- Selective catheterization codes separately billable in hemorrhage setting
Note: Use ONLY when indication is hemorrhage (M25.061–M25.069). Most payers reimburse 37244 + selective catheter codes for hemorrhagic indications without experimental designation.

## Payer Coverage Policies
Payer type filter (UI tabs): Medicare | Commercial | Medicaid

### Medicare (Traditional) — Partial Coverage — Moderate Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: No formal PA required — but verify coverage before scheduling
COVERAGE SUMMARY: No National Coverage Determination (NCD) or Local Coverage Determination (LCD) specific to GAE for OA. CMS reimburses 37242 under the general therapeutic embolization NCD (20.28) when medically reasonable and necessary. Selective catheter codes (36245–36248) are typically denied for MSK diagnoses.
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- Moderate-to-severe knee OA (KL Grade II–IV) documented on weight-bearing radiograph
- Failure of ≥6 months of conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs, corticosteroid injections)
- Not a surgical candidate OR patient declines TKA
- VAS pain score ≥5/10 at baseline
- Absence of active joint infection or severe vascular disease
PRACTICE TIP: Use ABN (Advanced Beneficiary Notice) form for Medicare patients before the procedure. Document medical necessity thoroughly in the operative note. Avoid billing 36245/36246 with OA diagnosis codes — high denial risk.

### Medicare Advantage — Variable — Verify — High Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: Prior authorization required by most MA plans
COVERAGE SUMMARY: Coverage varies significantly by plan. Some MA plans follow traditional Medicare policy; others apply commercial payer criteria (e.g., UHC MA, Humana MA may require additional documentation or deny as experimental).
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- All traditional Medicare criteria apply
- Additional plan-specific documentation may be required
- Some plans require peer-to-peer review before approval
PRACTICE TIP: Always call the MA plan to verify coverage before scheduling. Request the specific coverage policy in writing. Peer-to-peer review is highly effective for MA plan denials.

### Anthem / BCBS (most plans) — Experimental — Denied — Very High Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: N/A — procedure classified as experimental/investigational
COVERAGE SUMMARY: Anthem explicitly classifies GAE as experimental, investigational, and not medically necessary for knee pain or osteoarthritis. Coverage is denied under most Anthem and affiliated BCBS plans.
COVERAGE CRITERIA: (none listed)
PRACTICE TIP: Obtain a signed patient financial responsibility waiver before the procedure. Submit a formal appeal citing RCT data (Landers 2021) and the AOSSM/AAOS position statement. Some plans have overturned denials after peer-to-peer review with an IR physician.

### Aetna — Partial Coverage — Moderate Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: Prior authorization required
COVERAGE SUMMARY: Aetna includes OA knee diagnoses (M17.0–M17.9) and hemarthrosis (M25.061–M25.069) as covered diagnoses for embolization. No specific GAE policy exists — coverage is determined under general therapeutic embolization criteria. Verify with individual plan.
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- Documented moderate-to-severe knee OA with radiographic evidence
- Failure of conservative therapy (minimum 3–6 months)
- Clinical documentation of functional impairment
- Not a surgical candidate or patient declines surgery
PRACTICE TIP: Ask Aetna specifically whether "no PA required" means the service is covered or simply not tracked. Some Aetna plans may deny at claim level even without a PA requirement. Confirm coverage in writing.

### UnitedHealthcare — Variable — Verify — High Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: Prior authorization required — verify per plan
COVERAGE SUMMARY: UHC does not have a specific GAE policy. Coverage is adjudicated under general therapeutic embolization criteria. Vetting the PA request meticulously before the procedure is essential — do not assume coverage.
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- Documented clinical indication with imaging support
- Failure of conservative management
- Procedure performed by qualified interventional radiologist
- Outpatient or ambulatory surgical center setting
PRACTICE TIP: Submit a detailed PA request with clinical notes, imaging reports, and conservative treatment records. Request peer-to-peer review if initial PA is denied. Document that the procedure is being performed by a board-certified IR physician.

### Cigna — Variable — Verify — High Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: Prior authorization required
COVERAGE SUMMARY: Cigna coverage for GAE varies by plan and region. Some Cigna plans follow Anthem criteria (experimental designation); others may cover under general embolization policy. Verify individual plan policy.
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- Clinical documentation of OA severity and functional limitation
- Failure of conservative therapy
- Appropriate patient selection per published criteria
PRACTICE TIP: Contact Cigna medical policy department directly for the most current coverage determination. Peer-to-peer review is recommended for any initial denial.

### Medicaid (State-specific) — Variable — Verify — High Denial Risk
PA REQUIREMENT: Prior authorization required in most states
COVERAGE SUMMARY: Medicaid coverage for GAE varies significantly by state. Most state Medicaid programs do not have a specific GAE policy and adjudicate under general therapeutic embolization criteria. Some states (e.g., California Medi-Cal) may classify as experimental.
COVERAGE CRITERIA:
- State-specific medical necessity criteria apply
- Documentation of conservative treatment failure
- Procedure must be performed at a Medicaid-enrolled facility
PRACTICE TIP: Contact your state Medicaid program directly for coverage determination. Obtain written authorization before scheduling.

## Required Documentation Checklist

### Clinical Documentation
- Office visit notes documenting knee pain severity (VAS ≥5/10), duration (≥6 months), and functional limitation
- Orthopedic or primary care physician notes confirming OA diagnosis and conservative treatment history
- Documentation of failed conservative therapies: physical therapy (≥6 weeks), NSAIDs, corticosteroid injections, viscosupplementation
- Functional assessment scores: KOOS, WOMAC, or Oxford Knee Score at baseline
- Documentation that patient is not a surgical candidate OR has declined TKA after informed discussion

### Imaging
- Weight-bearing AP and lateral knee radiographs (within 12 months) — Kellgren-Lawrence Grade II–IV required
- MRI of the knee (within 12 months) — documenting cartilage loss, synovitis, or bone marrow edema
- Radiology reports for all imaging studies

### Procedure-Specific
- Procedure request letter from referring physician or interventional radiologist
- Signed informed consent documenting patient understanding of experimental status with some payers
- Patient financial responsibility waiver (for Medicare patients — ABN form; for commercial payers — plan-specific waiver)
- Facility accreditation documentation (if required by payer)

### Supporting Evidence (for appeals)
- Okuno Y et al., Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol 2017 — foundational prospective study
- Bagla S et al., J Vasc Interv Radiol 2020 — multicenter prospective trial (70% responder rate)
- Landers S et al., Cardiovasc Intervent Radiol 2021 — RCT demonstrating superiority over sham
- AOSSM/AAOS Position Statement 2023 — recognizes GAE as emerging minimally invasive option
- ACR Appropriateness Criteria 2022 — appropriate for moderate-to-severe OA refractory to conservative treatment
- SIR Standards of Practice 2022 — safety profile and technical success rates

## Denial Response Strategies

### Denial: Experimental / Investigational
Strategy: Submit Level 1 appeal with full RCT data (Landers 2021), multicenter prospective trial data (Bagla 2020), and AOSSM/AAOS 2023 position statement. Request peer-to-peer review with an interventional radiologist. Cite ACR Appropriateness Criteria 2022.
Expected outcome: Moderate — ~30–50% overturn rate with complete evidence package

### Denial: Not Medically Necessary
Strategy: Provide complete conservative treatment failure documentation (PT records, injection dates, medication trials). Include functional assessment scores (KOOS/WOMAC) demonstrating significant impairment. Document that surgical alternatives were considered and declined or contraindicated.
Expected outcome: Moderate-to-High — ~50–70% overturn rate with complete documentation

### Denial: Diagnosis-CPT Code Mismatch
Strategy: Confirm 37242 is the correct code for OA indication. Provide a detailed operative note explaining the clinical rationale. Consider requesting a predetermination letter from the payer before the procedure.
Expected outcome: High — ~70–80% resolution with correct coding and documentation

### Denial: No Prior Authorization
Strategy: Submit retroactive PA request with full clinical documentation. If denied retroactively, file a formal appeal citing medical urgency if applicable. Document that the procedure was performed in good faith based on payer guidance.
Expected outcome: Low-to-Moderate — retroactive PA approvals are difficult; prevention is key

## Patient Financial Responsibility Waivers
Because many payers classify GAE as experimental, a signed financial responsibility waiver is essential before the procedure. Use the Medicare ABN for traditional Medicare patients and the commercial waiver for all other payers.
